findings.title: Unchecked property access on mainHostDestinationCalendar crashes when destinationCalendar is empty or null
findings.body: In `EventManager.create`, `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` will set `mainHostDestinationCalendar` to `undefined` whenever `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or `[]`. On line 119, `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` accesses `.integration` without optional chaining (`?.`), throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` for any Google Meet booking where the host has no destination calendar configured.

findings.title: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition breaks organization slug assignment
findings.body: Line 151 changed `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, inverting the boolean condition in a file unrelated to `destinationCalendar`. When `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is `false`, newly created organizations will have neither `slug` nor `metadata.requestedSlug` set, leaving them without a slug; when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is `true`, `slug` is prematurely assigned before billing is completed.

findings.title: Co-hosts' destination calendars are dropped when the primary organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: Lines 1063-1067 set `evt.destinationCalendar` to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is defined. On line 1078, `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` becomes a no-op due to optional chaining on `null`, so if the primary host has no `destinationCalendar` configured, all other collective hosts' `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded and no events are created in their destination calendars.

findings.title: Fallback calendar lookup in updateEvent and deleteEvent can never match and leaves calendarId undefined
findings.body: In `updateEvent` (lines 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (lines 315-317), the fallback branch of `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`null`, `undefined`, or `""`). Comparing `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` in that branch compares a non-empty calendar ID string against a falsy value and always evaluates to `undefined`. In `updateEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is passed directly as `calendarId` without defaulting to `"primary"`, causing `calendar.events.update` to fail whenever `externalCalendarId` is not present on the booking reference.

findings.title: calendar.events.patch receives undefined calendarId when selectedCalendar is not found
findings.body: In `createEvent`, `selectedCalendar` (lines 147-149) is `undefined` when no `destinationCalendar` entry matches `credentialId` (for example, when `destinationCalendar` is empty or has a `null` `credentialId`). While `calendar.events.insert` on line 154 falls back with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`, `calendar.events.patch` on line 168 passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar` directly, which is `undefined` and causes patching the Google Meet hangout link into the event description to fail.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar services always use the first host's destinationCalendar instead of matching the credential
findings.body: In `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` (line 73), `LarkCalendarService.createEvent`/`createAttendees` (`packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` lines 128 and 164), and `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` line 156), the target calendar is selected via `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` rather than finding the entry matching the credential being used. In a collective booking where a secondary host uses Office365, Lark, or CalDAV, these services will use `event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId` (the primary host's calendar ID, potentially from a different provider like Google Calendar), causing event creation for the secondary host to fail or be skipped.

findings.title: updateAllCalendarEvents calls updateEvent even when credential lookup returns undefined
findings.body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents` (lines 511-542), if `reference.credentialId` is not in `this.calendarCredentials` and the database lookup either finds no credential or `credentialFromDB.app?.slug` is nullish, `credential` remains `undefined`. Unlike `createAllCalendarEvents` (line 369), line 542 does not guard with `if (credential)` before calling `updateEvent(credential, ...)`, which will throw a `TypeError` when `updateEvent` accesses `credential.appName`.

findings.title: Cancelling all remaining recurring bookings in a collective event ignores co-host credentials and references
findings.body: Inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` (lines 423-472), when `allRemainingBookings` is true for a recurring event, lines 449-461 ignore the resolved `calendar` for `reference.credentialId` and instead iterate over `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and only delete the first calendar reference (`updBooking.references.find(...)`) of each recurring booking. For collective bookings with multiple hosts, this repeats deletions on the primary organizer's calendar once per reference while never deleting the recurring event instances from the other hosts' calendars.
